title: Exercise Intensity Thresholds: Identifying the Boundaries of Sustainable Performance
authors: Keir DA, Fontana FY, Robertson TC, Murias JM, Paterson DH, Kowalchuk JM, Pogliaghi S
population: Twelve healthy men (27 +/- 3 yr) performing cycle ergometer tests for CP, MLSS, ramp-derived RCP and deoxyhemoglobin breakpoint
findings: Oxygen uptake at CP, RCP, MLSS and [HHb] breakpoint did not differ (3.29, 3.34, 3.27 and 3.41 L/min respectively).
Power output at RCP (262 W) and [HHb] breakpoint (273 W) was higher than at CP (226 W) and MLSS (223 W), which did not differ from each other.
The authors conclude the indices occur at the same VO2 and each provides a valid delineation between tolerable and intolerable constant-power exercise.
limitations: Twelve healthy young men on a cycle ergometer; not runners; RCP and CP were at the same VO2 but different power outputs, so the 'same threshold' conclusion is about VO2, not about the workload prescribed.
implications: Treat RCP/VT2 and CS as neighbouring but not identical markers of the upper sustainable boundary: when both RCP-type (HR, RPE) and CS estimates exist, expect different absolute workloads and keep both as ranges rather than forcing one value.
Supports using CS as the sustainable upper boundary rather than a lactate-defined value, but evidence is from cycling.
